Hi Emma —

Great to meet you and the Crestline team today. Quick recap from our 30-minute discovery so we have alignment and clear next steps: 

Summary of needs you shared:
- Use case: real-time conversational search + summarization for customer support (high context >512 tokens).
- Latency SLO: 95th percentile under 250ms for short prompts; okay to be higher for long-context workloads.
- Traffic: expected steady-state ~150 TPS with 300 TPS burst windows during peak hours.
- Token mix: average request ~600 tokens (prompt + response), ~20% very long sessions (~2k tokens).
- Data constraints: PII redaction required; would prefer VPC/private deployment for Prod but open to Dedicated pool for initial ramp.

Open qualification items we promised to confirm:
1) GPU recommendation (A100 vs H100) for your token mix and cost targets.
2) Concurrency settings & batching guidance for 150 TPS steady / 300 TPS bursts.
3) Fallback routing plan (Hosted API fallback if dedicated pool is saturated).
4) A short-capacity workbook to capture exact throughput/latency tradeoffs.

Action items / next steps:
- I will share a draft capacity workbook (attached) and our initial sizing options for Dedicated (A100-family and H100-family) by EOD tomorrow. (Vanessa)
- Emma / Crestline to confirm whether Prod must be private VPC from day one or can start in Dedicated with a VPC migration plan. (Crestline)
- Karthik will weigh in on autoscale/fallback constraints and the recommended concurrency ceiling for your SLOs. (Karthik)

Attachments: crestline_rfp.pdf (from your procurement) — thanks for sending.

If this looks right, can we lock a 45-minute follow-up on Wednesday 8/18 to walk the workbook together? I’ll include a quick decision matrix to make the hosted vs dedicated vs private tradeoffs explicit.

Thanks,

Emma —

Thank you for the quick responses. Attached is a first-pass capacity_workbook.xlsx (stub) and my initial recommendations below. I kept it concise so we can iterate on the call on 8/18.

Short answers up front:
- GPU recommendation: For your mix (avg ~600 tokens, ~20% long sessions), H100 provides ~15–25% lower p95 latency for long-context model runs and better throughput for 2k+ token sessions. A100 is a lower-cost baseline and still reasonable if you quantize aggressively and accept slightly higher p95 for long-context calls.
- Concurrency / batching: We recommend targeting a per-GPU sustained concurrency of 18–24 model streams for H100 and 12–16 for A100 for the base model (non-quantized). With Redwood continuous batching and prefix caching enabled, that mapping supports ~150 TPS steady with headroom for short bursts if you enable burst slots.
- Burst strategy: Configure reserved Dedicated pool at 1.2x steady (to cover common variance) and enable a burst policy to pull from our hosted spare capacity for 2–10 minute spikes. We’ll configure automatic fallback to hosted endpoints for non-sensitive workloads; for VPC/Private Prod we’ll set up a documented manual escalation path to add temporary slots.

Sizing scenarios (high-level):
- Option A (Cost conservative): A100s, quantized 4-bit model profile, reserved pool sized for 160 TPS steady, burst to hosted for short spikes. Expected unit cost: lower, but p95 for 2k-token runs higher.
- Option B (Performance priority): H100s, mixed precision (no quantize for long-context models), reserved pool sized for 200 TPS steady with 300 TPS burst slots. Higher cost, better p95 for long sessions.
- Option C (Hybrid path to Private): Start with Dedicated H100 for pilot, run Prod in Dedicated for first 3 months while completing VPC onboarding and KMS integration, then migrate to Private VPC for final Prod cutover.

Attached: capacity_workbook.xlsx (please fill in expected concurrent sessions by region and token percentiles; I included a few example rows). Karthik / Marissa — please skim the workbook before our call and flag any gaps on autoscale/ops runbook.

Do you want me to include a simple cost-comparison sheet (A100 vs H100) for the 12-month commit? I can have that ready before the call.

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz
Account Exec, Redwood Inference

Looping in with a few ops notes to make the pilot smoother: 

- Autoscale & burst implementation: We can set up a scheduled burst window tied to your marketing calendar (pre-authorized) so you don’t have to request manual capacity during predictable blasts. For ad-hoc spikes, we’ll set a policy that automatically routes non-PII traffic to Hosted and alerts the on-call if private workloads exceed the reserved pool for >5 minutes.
- Concurrency ceiling: Start with conservative ceiling (18 streams per H100 equivalent) and run a short synthetic load to validate p95. If results show consistent headroom, we can dial to 22–24. We’ll include telemetry hooks in the workbook for per-GPU util, queue depth, and per-route fallbacks.
- Migration notes: For Private VPC migration, required items: KMS integration, private endpoints, and an audit log handoff plan; timeline estimate 6–8 weeks after start of Dedicated pilot.

I’ll prepare a 1-page ops runbook snippet to attach to the workbook before the Wednesday call.

-Karthik
